operation.description: Solve a bounded exact rational LP with labeled LE, EQ, and GE rows, finite bounds, and free variables. Results retain the original source coordinates and replayed optimality, Farkas, or recession evidence; private slack and sign-split columns never appear on the wire.

examples.description: Minimize x subject to x>=1; all rows and bounds are closed exact rationals.
examples.name: bounded_inequality_lp

CanonicalRational.description: A reduced rational whose denominator is positive and whose zero is 0/1.

den.description: Positive canonical decimal denominator; together with num it must be reduced, and integers use den='1'.
den.title: Den

num.description: Canonical decimal numerator of the reduced rational.
num.title: Num

GeneralFormRationalLinearProgram.description:
Optimize an exact rational objective with rows and finite bounds.

A null bound is absent; two null bounds make a variable free.  All rows and
bounds are closed, so strict feasibility is expressed with a caller-owned
explicit margin variable rather than an implicit strict relation.

constraints.description: Ordered labeled LE, EQ, or GE rows in original coordinates.
constraints.title: Constraints

variables.description: Ordered original-coordinate variables with explicit closed bounds.
variables.title: Variables

RationalLinearConstraint.description: One labeled exact rational affine relation in source coordinates.

coefficients.description: Exact row coefficients in the enclosing program variable order.
coefficients.title: Coefficients

label.description: Unique source identity for this relation, not display-only text.
label.title: Label

relation.description: LE means a*x <= rhs, EQ means equality, and GE means a*x >= rhs.

output_schema.description:
A canonical exact outcome for a general-form rational LP.

Dual multipliers use the source objective sense.  For minimization, LE
row and upper-bound multipliers are nonpositive while GE and lower-bound
multipliers are nonnegative; the signs reverse for maximization.  An
infeasibility certificate instead has LE/nonnegative and GE/nonpositive
row multipliers, and satisfies its source Farkas balance directly.
output_schema.title: GeneralRationalLinearProgramResult
